== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (8 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]]) [[Cookbook:Beef#Brisket|beef brisket]], trimmed to ¼ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] of fat
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 tbsp black [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]], cracked
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] apple [[Cookbook:Cider Vinegar|cider vinegar]]
* ¾ cup yellow [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]], divided
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Garlic Powder|garlic powder]]
* ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Paprika|paprika]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Hot Sauce|hot sauce]]
* 9 hamburger buns
* 3 tbsp [[Cookbook:Molasses|molasses]]
* Large mesquite chunks

== Procedure ==
#Combine hot sauce, molasses, vinegar, and ¼ cup mustard. Pour into a spray bottle and set aside.
#Coat brisket with ½ cup of the mustard. Set aside.
#Combine seasonings and salt. Press mixture into both sides of brisket. Refrigerate overnight.
#The next day, heat up a smoker to 200°F with the mesquite chunks. Add brisket and cook 9 hours, spraying every 3 hours with vinegar mixture, and changing wood as needed to keep temperature at 200°F.
#Remove brisket from smoker and let rest ½ hour. Separate along the fat line and [[Cookbook:Slicing|slice]] thinly across the grain.
#Finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chop]] slices and toss with remaining vinegar mixture. Place 1/9 into each bun and serve warm.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you don't have a smoker, just preheat your [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 190°F. Place ¾ cup soaked mesquite chips in the bottom of a roasting pan and add a rack and your rubbed brisket. Cover tightly with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|foil]] and cook the same.
